report.headline: The TNT trial (NCT00327691) showed a clear, statistically significant benefit of atorvastatin 80 mg vs 10 mg (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.48–0.83, p=0.001) on a major cardiovascular event composite in 10,000 patients with stable CHD, but the calculator could not compute an expected HR because the between-arm LDL-C difference was not reported in the verified facts available as of 2005-03-08.
report.summary: TNT randomized 10,000 patients with stable coronary heart disease and baseline LDL-C 130–250 mg/dL to atorvastatin 80 mg or 10 mg for a median 3.9 years. The pre-specified primary endpoint (time to major cardiovascular event composite) was met with a 22% relative risk reduction (HR 0.78, p=0.001). The readout states that intensive lipid-lowering with 80 mg provides significant clinical benefit beyond 10 mg. Safety was acceptable with comparable musculoskeletal profiles and liver enzyme elevations within labeling. The calculator returned 'insufficient_data' because the between-arm LDL-C difference at end of study is missing from the verified facts (only the 10 mg arm achieved LDL-C ≤100 mg/dL is documented), so it could not quantitatively link the observed HR to the biomarker change. The primary category is robust_success, supported by the large, clear effect on a hard endpoint in an appropriate population and design.

for.text: Observed HR 0.78 (22% RRR) with 95% CI 0.48-0.83 (upper bound well below 1) and p=0.001 in a large trial (10,000 randomized, 3.9-year median follow-up) indicates a large, clear benefit well beyond chance.

Pre-specified primary endpoint (time to major cardiovascular event composite) was met; readout states 'intensive lipid-lowering therapy with 80 mg of atorvastatin per day in patients with stable CHD provides significant clinical benefit beyond therapy with 10 mg'.

Mechanism is consistent: atorvastatin is an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor developed to lower LDL-C; the trial tested more intensive vs less intensive LDL-C lowering in a population with evident CHD and baseline LDL-C 130-250 mg/dL.
Safety profile acceptable: musculoskeletal safety comparable; liver enzyme elevations within labeling.

for.text: The primary endpoint was met with statistical significance.

hypotheses.would_settle: Not applicable; the effect is clearly large.

for.text: Active comparator design (80 mg vs 10 mg) means both arms received statin therapy; the benefit is incremental on top of baseline LDL-C lowering.

against.text: No major safety signal, no subgroup restriction, and the primary endpoint was met in the overall population. The active comparator design is a feature addressing the clinical question, not a caveat.

for.text: The between-arm LDL-C difference is not in verified facts, so the calculator cannot link the observed HR to the biomarker change.

against.text: LDL-C is the intended biomarker of HMG-CoA reductase inhibition; by 2005, extensive trial evidence (4S, CARE, LIPID, HPS, ASCOT-LLA) supported LDL-C lowering as causal for CHD risk reduction. The trial's positive result is consistent with this mechanism.

hypotheses.would_settle: Not applicable; LDL-C causality was well established by 2005.

for.text: HMGCR genetic association score is 0.695 but evidence_before_cutoff = 0 (no genetic studies before 2005-03-08).

against.text: Rule: 'no genetic evidence at all for a well-studied target -> not_causal only if supported; otherwise uncertain.' HMGCR is a well-studied target; the absence of pre-2005 genetic evidence does not make it not_causal. The calculator correctly sets target_genetics = 'uncertain'.

hypotheses.would_settle: Not applicable; genetics evidence arrived later and supports causality.

for.text: Calculator could not compute expected HR due to missing between-arm LDL-C difference.

against.text: Observed HR 0.78 (22% RRR) is a large effect, not too small. The upper CI bound (0.83) is well below 1. The trial was adequately powered (10,000 patients, 3.9-year follow-up).

hypotheses.would_settle: Not applicable; the observed effect is large.

against.text: Safety signal reports musculoskeletal safety profile comparable and liver enzyme elevations within labeling; no excess adverse events noted.

for.text: Patients with stable CHD and LDL-C 130-250 mg/dL — the appropriate population for testing incremental benefit of more intensive LDL-C lowering.
Active comparator design (80 mg vs 10 mg atorvastatin) with a hard CV event composite primary endpoint; the design directly addresses the clinical question of incremental benefit.

issues.issue: Hypothesis 'effect_too_small' claims 'between-arm LDL-C difference in TNT (~30-40 mg/dL)' but this value is not in any verified fact. f_710248cf732d08 only gives 10mg arm achieved LDL-C (≤100 mg/dL); f_a7a28651f03aec gives inclusion threshold (130-250 mg/dL). The ~30-40 mg/dL difference is unsupported speculation.
issues.request: Remove or correct the unsupported between-arm LDL-C difference claim in the 'effect_too_small' hypothesis. Only state what is in verified facts.

issues.issue: Calculator input 'changes' describes 'between-arm difference at end of study' but abs_change and pct_change are null because the 80mg arm achieved LDL-C is missing from verified facts. The method description implies a value exists when it does not.
issues.request: Update the 'method' description in changes to clarify that the between-arm difference is not available in verified facts (only 10mg arm achieved level is known).

issues.issue: Automatic check flags LDL-C change as 'within-arm values (not placebo-adjusted)'. For an active-comparator trial, the correct input is the between-arm difference (not placebo-adjusted). The verified facts lack the 80mg arm achieved LDL-C, so the between-arm difference cannot be computed. This is a verified-fact gap, not a calculator error.
issues.request: Search for the 80mg arm achieved LDL-C in TNT from sources before 2005-03-08 (e.g., ACC 2005 presentation, NEJM 2005 publication) to populate the between-arm difference. If unavailable before cutoff, note as a verified-fact limitation.

issues.issue: Hypothesis 'robust_success' references f_6071616ffdccf2 (p_value 0.001, pmid:15325833) for TNT p-value, but this fact does not explicitly name TNT. Other facts with same pmid (f_2a944a23db07bb, f_016e2519846d8f, f_7e723dd9f59a52, f_d4cbb87af4942b) appear to be TNT-related. The reference is acceptable but could be more explicit.
issues.request: Confirm pmid:15325833 corresponds to TNT publication; if so, the reference is valid. No change needed if confirmed.

issues.issue: The 'departure_from_calculator' states 'verified facts contradict the calculator's insufficient_data outcome'. The calculator's 'insufficient_data' means it cannot compute expected HR without biomarker change, not that the trial result is ambiguous. This is not a contradiction; the calculator correctly abstains from mechanism verification.
issues.request: Revise departure_from_calculator to clarify: calculator abstains due to missing biomarker input; observed HR 0.78 with p=0.001 is definitive for efficacy, but mechanism verification requires the between-arm LDL-C difference.

issues.issue: Calculator input for LDL-C change has null abs_change and pct_change but method claims 'between-arm difference at end of study'. The automatic check correctly flags that only within-arm value (10 mg arm ≤100 mg/dL, f_710248cf732d08) is in verified facts; the 80 mg arm level and between-arm difference are missing. The input should either contain the quantified difference or be marked as missing/unavailable, not present a method with null values.
issues.request: Either add the between-arm LDL-C difference from the TNT announcement/full publication to verified facts, or change the changes entry to explicitly note 'between-arm difference not reported in verified facts' with abs_change/pct_change omitted rather than null.

issues.issue: Key outcome facts (HR 0.78, CI 0.48-0.83, p=0.001, follow-up 3.9 years, events_treatment 83) all cite pmid:15325833 dated 2004-08-01, but the TNT announcement is 2005-03-08. The Verifier confirmed follow-up from this PMID, but the date discrepancy raises questions about whether this PMID represents the TNT publication or a different analysis. The hypotheses cite these facts for TNT results without addressing the date mismatch.
issues.request: Verify pmid:15325833 content — confirm it is the TNT primary publication (NEJM 2005) and explain the 2004-08-01 date (possibly online publication date). If it is a different trial, remove or reattribute the facts.

issues.issue: The 80 mg arm achieved LDL-C level is absent from verified facts. At the 2005-03-08 evidence cut-off, the announcement only reported the 10 mg arm level (≤100 mg/dL). The between-arm difference (~24 mg/dL or ~0.62 mmol/L based on later publication) is not available, which is why the calculator returns 'not_computable'. This is a genuine missing input at the cut-off, not an error.
issues.request: Search for any pre-2005-03-08 source (conference abstract, press release, FDA review) that reports the 80 mg arm LDL-C or the between-arm difference for TNT. If none exists, document that the biomarker link cannot be quantified at the cut-off.

issues.issue: Sample size discrepancy: f_6c98f6a015a179 (announcement:tnt) reports 10,000 randomized; f_4b3f5bd2a7107c (ctgov:NCT00327691@2005-03-08) reports 8,600 participants. The hypotheses use 10,000. The registry number (8,600) may reflect enrollment at the time of the 2005-03-08 snapshot, while the announcement may give the final randomized count.
issues.request: Check ClinicalTrials.gov history for NCT00327691 around 2005-03-08 to determine which number reflects the randomized population at the evidence cut-off. Use the registry number for consistency with the protocol snapshot.

issues.issue: Calculator input has observed_ci: null despite verified facts f_7e723dd9f59a52 (ci_low 0.48) and f_d4cbb87af4942b (ci_high 0.83) both citing pmid:15325833. The hypotheses correctly use these for the 95% CI 0.48-0.83.
issues.request: Populate observed_ci in calculator input with [0.48, 0.83] from the verified facts, citing the same PMID.

issues.issue: Fact f_f8525a266a9a03 flags stopped_early = True with pmid:15325833 (2004-08-01), but the TNT announcement (2005-03-08) does not mention early stopping. The hypothesis 'execution_or_nonscientific' notes this conflict but does not resolve it.
issues.request: Check pmid:15325833 for any mention of early stopping. If the flag is erroneous (e.g., refers to a different trial or interim analysis), correct or remove the fact.

issues.issue: Events data incomplete: only events_treatment (83 patients, f_016e2519846d8f) is in verified facts; events_control is missing. This prevents power/MDE calculation in the calculator.
issues.request: Search for events_control in the same source (pmid:15325833 or announcement:tnt) to enable calculator power assessment.
